chunks.arabic_text: ٥ - إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْعَلَاءِ، الْمَدَنِيُّ.
لَا يُعْرَفُ إِلَّا بِمَا يُنْسَبُ إِلَيْهِ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ الْبَلَوِيُّ.

translations.en: Not recognized except for what is attributed to him by 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi.

chunks.arabic_text: وَيُنْسَبُ إِلَى أَبِيهِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْعَلَاءِ عُمَارَةَ بْنِ زَيْدٍ.

translations.en: His father, 'Ubaydullah ibn al-'Ala, is related to 'Amara ibn Zayd.

chunks.arabic_text: وَمَا يُسْنَدُ إِلَيْهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِدَ الْمُتَهَافِتَ.

translations.en: Chains of narrations do not go back to him but through the corrupt and confused.

chunks.arabic_text: وَأَظُنُّهُ اسْمًا مَوْضُوعًا عَلَى غَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ.

translations.en: I suspect that his name has been assigned to more than one.

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights the critical scrutiny applied to Ibrahim ibn 'Ubaydullah al-Madani, whose reliability hinges on the single narrator 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi. The classification of his narrations as 'fasad' (defective) and 'tahauf' (confused) reflects the Shia tradition's emphasis on precise chain verification to preserve doctrinal integrity. Furthermore, the suspicion that the name is 'mawdu' (fabricated or applied to multiple individuals) underscores the methodological rigor used to distinguish authentic transmission from potential conflation or forgery in early hadith literature.
en.seo_question: Who is Ibrahim ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn al-'Ala and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?
